newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-ANALYSIS OF KAFELNIKOV V PIOLINE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ANALYSIS OF KAFELNIKOV V PIOLINE.

text.p: Analysis of Friday's French Open men's singles third round match between third seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia and France's Cedric Pioline, won 7-5 6-4 6-7 (3-7) 1-6 6-4 by Kafelnikov.

Both players had lost their serve twice and were heading for a tie-break when Pioline gave Kafelnikov a break point with a clumsy unforced error in the 12th game. Pioline then hit a backhand long, allowing the Russian to take the set.
The telling break came in the sixth game, giving Kafelnikov a 4-2 lead. A slam volley on set point allowed him to go two sets up.
Both players held serve throughout the set which ended in a tie-break. Pioline took it 7-3 with a superb forehand winner.
Pioline moved on top of a tiring Kafelnikov, building a 3-0 lead in just 10 minutes. The Frenchman underlined his determination by winning the last game to love with an ace on set point.

Pioline came close to victory with a break for a 4-3 lead. But he lost the following game, double-faulting on break point and Kafelnikov then took the next two games with Pioline hitting a backhand long on match point.
